subject: Religionskunskap
title: The Abrahamic religions
sourceSummary: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are known as the Abrahamic religions. You learn what they have in common, which scriptures and buildings they have, and what the most important differences are.

questions.prompt: Which three religions are called the Abrahamic religions?
questions.opener: They have all arisen in the Middle East and count the same man as a forefather.
choices: Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism
Judaism, Hinduism and Islam
Judaism, Christianity and Islam
Christianity, Buddhism and Islam
questions.explanation: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called Abrahamic religions because all three regard Abraham as a central figure and arose in the Middle East. Hinduism and Buddhism instead arose in India and are counted as Eastern religions.

questions.prompt: What do Judaism, Christianity and Islam have in common?
questions.opener: Think about how many gods they count, and which figure ties them together.
choices: They are monotheistic - belief in a single god - and all three see Abraham as an important figure
They have exactly the same sacred scripture
They all use the same building for worship
They all have their most important centre in Rome
questions.explanation: What they share is monotheism (belief in a single god), Abraham as a forefather, sacred scriptures, prophets and a strong emphasis on how people should live. The scriptures and buildings, on the other hand, differ, and Rome is a centre mainly for the Catholic Church.

questions.opener: According to Islam it was conveyed to the prophet Muhammad.
choices: The Torah
The Qur'an
The New Testament
The Talmud
questions.explanation: The Qur'an is Islam's sacred scripture, and within Islam it is believed to be God's word conveyed to the prophet Muhammad. The Torah and the Talmud belong to Judaism, while the New Testament is part of the Christian Bible.

questions.prompt: What is Judaism's most important sacred scripture called?
questions.opener: It consists of the first five books of what Christians call the Old Testament.
choices: The Qur'an
The Vedas
The New Testament
The Torah
questions.explanation: The Torah, the five Books of Moses, is Judaism's most important scripture and forms part of the wider scripture known as the Tanakh. The Vedas belong to Hinduism, and the New Testament is Christian - Judaism does not count the New Testament as scripture.

questions.prompt: Which option correctly pairs the religion with its place of worship?
questions.opener: Three different words: one for Judaism, one for Christianity and one for Islam.
choices: Judaism: mosque · Christianity: synagogue · Islam: church
Judaism: church · Christianity: mosque · Islam: synagogue
Judaism: synagogue · Christianity: church · Islam: mosque
Judaism: temple · Christianity: mosque · Islam: synagogue
questions.explanation: Judaism's place of worship is the synagogue, Christianity's is the church, and Islam's is the mosque. The word temple is used within Judaism mainly for the old Temple in Jerusalem, which was destroyed in 70 AD and of which the Western Wall is a remnant.

questions.prompt: How is Jesus viewed within the three Abrahamic religions?
questions.opener: All three mention him, but they assign him different roles.
choices: All three religions believe that Jesus is the Son of God
None of the three religions mentions Jesus
Only Judaism counts Jesus as a prophet
In Christianity, Jesus is believed to be the Son of God, in Islam he is counted as one of the prophets, and in Judaism he is not seen as the Messiah
questions.explanation: The view of Jesus is one of the clearest differences: Christianity sees him as the Son of God and the Messiah, Islam as an important prophet but not as the Son of God, and Judaism is still waiting for the Messiah. So it is not the case that all three share the same view.

questions.prompt: Explain why Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called Abrahamic religions, and give examples of both shared features and differences.
questions.opener: Start with the name, then take the similarities, and finish with the clearest differences.
questions.answer: The name comes from Abraham, whom all three religions regard as a central figure and forefather. What they share is that they are monotheistic - all three believe in a single god - and that they have sacred scriptures, prophets and rules for how people should live. They have also arisen in the same part of the world and regard Jerusalem as a holy city. The differences concern, among other things, which scripture is sacred (the Tanakh with the Torah, the Bible, the Qur'an), which building people gather in (synagogue, church, mosque), and what role Jesus has. Comparing them helps us understand both why they sometimes resemble each other and why they are three separate religions.
steps: The name comes from Abraham, who is regarded as a forefather within all three religions.
Shared: monotheism (a single god), sacred scriptures, prophets and ethical rules for life.
Shared: all three arose in the Middle East and see Jerusalem as a holy city.
Differences: sacred scriptures (Tanakh/Torah, the Bible, the Qur'an) and buildings (synagogue, church, mosque).
Differences: the view of Jesus - Son of God in Christianity, a prophet in Islam, not the Messiah in Judaism.

questions.prompt: Summarise Judaism, Christianity and Islam side by side.
questions.opener: Compare religion by religion: scripture, building, leader, holy day and central figures.
questions.answer: Shared: monotheism (a single god) · Abraham as forefather · sacred scriptures and prophets · Jerusalem as a holy city · Judaism: sacred scripture the Tanakh, most important is the Torah (five Books of Moses) · building the synagogue · leader the rabbi · holy day the Sabbath from Friday evening to Saturday evening · important figures Abraham and Moses · according to Judaism the Messiah has not yet come · Christianity: sacred scripture the Bible (Old and New Testaments) · building the church · leader a priest or pastor · holy day Sunday · according to Christian belief Jesus is the Son of God who rose from the dead · branches Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant · Islam: sacred scripture the Qur'an · building the mosque · leader the imam · holy day Friday with communal prayer · according to Islam Muhammad is the final prophet and Jesus is one of the prophets · branches Sunni and Shia · The biggest difference between them: the view of Jesus and of which scripture is God's final message.
